To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a serum CA19-19 response of 85 percent or higher after neoadjuvent therapy is associated with improved survival and is predictive of T-stage reduction in patients with pancreatic adenocarcimona.

the optimal serum CA19-19 response threshold for pancreatic adenocanceroma patients receiving neoadjuvant treatment was 85% or more and this response correlated with a 25% or more decrease in tumor size.
a serum CA19-19 response of 85 percent or higher is the best cutoff point for predicting survival in pancreatic cancer patients who have undergone neoadjuvant treatment.

the study of the relationship between the level of the tumor marker CA19-9 before and after the treatment of pancreatic cancer and the prognosis of pancreatic cancer.
the use of a serum biomarker (CA 19-9) to predict response to therapy and survival in patients with pancreatic adenocarcimoma.

the serum CA19-19 response after NT in pancreatic adenocarcnoma is a strong predictor of tumor size reduction and survival.
